East London Tavern Tragedy

By: Sipha Kema | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The devastating death of 21 minors at an East London Tavern shines the spotlight on the country's underage drinking crisis

Unique Selling Point:
The continuous crisis of underage drinking in the country and the mushrooming of taverns in the townships has come under the spotlight after 21 underage tavern patrons died in the early hours on Sunday.

Alcohol abuse is rife in South Africa, underage drinking has seemingly become a norm in communities especially in townships.

The question of parenting and the law have also come into play. How does a 13 year old leave home for the entire night? What do the by-laws saying regarding the issuing of liquor licenses for establishments such as Enyobeni Tavern?

Who is responsible?



Summary:
An urgent issue of underage drinking and mushrooming taverns in the townships has come under the spotlight after 20 underage tavern patrons have died in the early hours on Sunday.
According to the residents and parents, waiting to identify their children, their children had said to be attending an All Black Party celebrating the end of exams, Pens down. Some parents are looking for minors as young as 13 years old.

This has seemingly become a norm in the South African townships where children as young as 13 years are out all night with the parents knowledge. Underage drinking itself has become somewhat “acceptable” as most of the establishments in the townships have underage patrons. Enyobeni is one of many taverns in East London known to allow minors entry, areas such as Duncan Village and Mdantsane are also known to break the law.

Another key issue is the mushrooming of taverns in residential areas, such as Enyobeni Tavern in Scenery Park. It leaves a lot of questions as far as the issuing of the liquor licenses and the municipalities implementing the by-laws. Neighbors within less than 20m proximity have complained about the noise and trading times of the tavern. It is also said the metro police who are meant to patrol such areas at night, are hardly seen, allowing chaos to ensue.

After identifying their children, parents and families were seen distraught most stating not being able to afford to bury their children. Some parents are calling for the closure of Enyobeni Tavern which was later temporarily closed by authorities.

The cause of death is yet to be released by the forensic unit, the officials have however ruled out a stampede as the cause of death.

As the days continue, the mystery surrounding the deaths of the 21 minors deepens.

Further information:
Underage drinking and the failure to implement by-laws by municipalities have put minors at risk, it also assists in the rise of this crisis.

There are many questions which need answers that could help such incidents from occuring.

The Enyobeni Tavern owner how does his establishment have a liquor license yet does not meet the requirements? The security at his establishment? The different stories surrounding the deaths of the patrons.

The Eastern Cape Liquor License Board, on what grounds do establishments like Enyobeni Tavern get awarded liquor licenses? Seeing the tavern now, does the board believe Enyobeni should have a trading liquor license?

The municipality, the responsibility of enforcing by-laws in these communities. What is going to happen to similar establishments in these areas?

All these contribute to the growing issue in question.

Clip name?

VO: Police are still investigating the cause of the deaths, but one question lingers: will the Enyobeni tragedy finally lead to a clampdown on underage drinking or will life continue as though 21 children didn’t just lose theirs?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The devastating death of 21 minors at an East London Tavern shines the spotlight on the country's underage drinking crisis
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The continuous crisis of underage drinking in the country and the mushrooming of taverns in the townships has come under the spotlight after 21 underage tavern patrons died in the early hours on Sunday. Alcohol abuse is rife in South Africa, underage drinking has seemingly become a norm in communities especially in townships. The question of parenting and the law have also come into play. How does a 13 year old leave home for the entire night? What do the by-laws saying regarding the issuing of liquor licenses for establishments such as Enyobeni Tavern? Who is responsible?
metadata.Summary: An urgent issue of underage drinking and mushrooming taverns in the townships has come under the spotlight after 20 underage tavern patrons have died in the early hours on Sunday. According to the residents and parents, waiting to identify their children, their children had said to be attending an All Black Party celebrating the end of exams, Pens down. Some parents are looking for minors as young as 13 years old. This has seemingly become a norm in the South African townships where children as young as 13 years are out all night with the parents knowledge. Underage drinking itself has become somewhat “acceptable” as most of the establishments in the townships have underage patrons. Enyobeni is one of many taverns in East London known to allow minors entry, areas such as Duncan Village and Mdantsane are also known to break the law. Another key issue is the mushrooming of taverns in residential areas, such as Enyobeni Tavern in Scenery Park. It leaves a lot of questions as far as the issuing of the liquor licenses and the municipalities implementing the by-laws. Neighbors within less than 20m proximity have complained about the noise and trading times of the tavern. It is also said the metro police who are meant to patrol such areas at night, are hardly seen, allowing chaos to ensue. After identifying their children, parents and families were seen distraught most stating not being able to afford to bury their children. Some parents are calling for the closure of Enyobeni Tavern which was later temporarily closed by authorities. The cause of death is yet to be released by the forensic unit, the officials have however ruled out a stampede as the cause of death. As the days continue, the mystery surrounding the deaths of the 21 minors deepens.
metadata.Further information: Underage drinking and the failure to implement by-laws by municipalities have put minors at risk, it also assists in the rise of this crisis. There are many questions which need answers that could help such incidents from occuring. The Enyobeni Tavern owner how does his establishment have a liquor license yet does not meet the requirements? The security at his establishment? The different stories surrounding the deaths of the patrons. The Eastern Cape Liquor License Board, on what grounds do establishments like Enyobeni Tavern get awarded liquor licenses? Seeing the tavern now, does the board believe Enyobeni should have a trading liquor license? The municipality, the responsibility of enforcing by-laws in these communities. What is going to happen to similar establishments in these areas? All these contribute to the growing issue in question.
